title: Small algebraic integers and Frobenius prime sums
summary: The determinant argument in recent proofs of Landau–Siegel zero exclusion compares the size of a nonzero integer with its divisibility by inert primes. We observe that the same comparison applies to every Frobenius class in a finite Galois extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, bounding its weighted prime count in terms of the supply of small algebraic integers. For each fixed field, the resulting height bound implies a weighted Chebotarev theorem whose only analytic inputs are the elementary Chebyshev and Mertens estimates.
